newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Socialists propose 35-hour work week by law.
newsitem.headline: French Socialists propose 35-hour work week by law.

text.p: France's opposition Socialist party will promise to cut the working week to 35 hours and create 700,000 jobs for young people at cost of about 50 billion francs ($8.6 billion), Socialist policy-maker Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Friday.

The Socialists are due to unveil their manifesto for the May 25-June 1 parliamentary election later on Friday and Strauss-Kahn said in a newspaper interview they would propose to cut the working week by law within three years. ($ = 5.809 French Francs)

Strauss-Kahn told business daily La Tribune the Socialists wanted to create 350,000 jobs in the public sector, by getting local authorities to offer young people five-year contracts on a full-time basis, paying at least the national minimum wage.

This plan would cost around 35 billion francs, he said. The state would finance these jobs where it was a direct employer or else foot 80 percent of the bill, with some of the money coming from the supression of certain employment incentive schemes.
It would propose subsidies to help create another 350,000 jobs in the private sector at a cost of around 15 billion francs, he said.
